chapter_note: This chapter is largely an exhortative homily on unity, using Light/Darkness as exempla and then directly addressing the community. Only small fragments preserve an older cosmological claim (unity/order in the Light; division in the Darkness). The extended comparison to "the kingdom of this world" and the second-person imperatives mark later application/pastoral expansion.

paragraphs.core_text: [Now as to what affects the] Light, behold, at the beginning the Darkness was strong against it; [ ... ] no disunity [ ... ] exists in the Light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic/dialogue frame attribution: "Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples:"
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with a formulaic frame marker identifying the speaker and audience (late compilation frame), but the remaining sentence makes an impersonal cosmological claim about the Light’s undivided nature (cosmos→cosmos), consistent with older teaching tone despite lacunae.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] how far [ ... the Lig]ht that came forth from [ ... ] in that place in a [ ... ] alone [ ... ] ⟨p.128⟩ the greatness of the Light with one another for ever, and nor did one of them transgress the command and order that his brother had entrusted to him forever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: No frame/citation/exhortation; describes intra-Light order and concord as an eternal condition (cosmic polity). Though "command and order" could be moralized diction, the mapping remains internal to the realm of Light (cosmos→cosmos).

paragraphs.core_text: However, the Darkness, the enemy, was doomed and overcome; because of the arising of disharmony it was divided within itself. Even the kingdom was divided within itself; [and] ev[en] the [powers, who had] left their abyss behind and come up fo[llow-ing] it, were doomed because of the disunity that was present in all of them. The Darkness was destroyed, and its other powers were humiliated,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed final comparative/application clause that reaches outside the cosmic system: "because the p[ower] of that first light functions in the same way as the kingdom of this world."
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins as cosmological mechanism (Darkness self-divides through disharmony), but pivots to an explicit analogy with "the kingdom of this world" (cosmos→contemporary-world comparison), signaling later applicative expansion.

Continues the kingdom/party-of-associates analogy in general terms ("associates in the m]ystery," glory, rivalry), without systematic cosmological mapping; reads as rhetorical application rather than substrate exposition.
Further develops the same moral-political analogy (condemnation/humiliation of the other kingdom). The paragraph functions as homiletic application rather than describing a fixed cosmic architecture.
Direct second-person exhortation ("you yourselves") about unity to conquer Sin; this is application/pastoral address to the community, not impersonal cosmological teaching.
Second-person warning and imperative tone ("Should you be divided... may it not happen!")—a pastoral consequence statement using Sin as oppressor.
Imperative exhortation ("Neither be divided...") with triumphal promises; fully applicative/community-directed rather than substrate description.
